back: A tag is a mutable pointer anyone with push rights can move. A digest (`sha256:...`) is the content hash of a manifest/index — immutable.
`aws ecr get-login-password --region <r> | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <acct>.dkr.ecr.<r>.amazonaws.com` (token valid 12 h; the repository must exist).
The files sent to the builder (the directory passed to `docker build`, minus `.dockerignore`). `COPY` can only read from it.
Speed (small context, fewer cache busts) and safety/correctness (no `.env`, `.git` or host `node_modules` with wrong-platform binaries in the image).
Exec `CMD ["node","app.js"]` runs the binary directly (gets signals, no shell needed, no `$VAR` expansion). Shell `CMD node app.js` runs `/bin/sh -c ...`.
Final command = ENTRYPOINT + CMD. `docker run img args` replaces CMD; `--entrypoint` replaces ENTRYPOINT (and clears CMD).

front: What must an entrypoint script end with?
back: `exec "$@"` — so the CMD replaces the shell as PID 1 and receives signals.
ARG: build-time only (`--build-arg`), recorded in history when used by RUN, scoped to a stage. ENV: build and runtime, stored in the image config. Neither is for secrets.
Parent layer + instruction text (+ build args used); for COPY/ADD also file content checksums (not mtimes). After the first miss, all later steps in the stage rebuild.
`COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` → `RUN npm ci` → `COPY` source → `RUN npm run build`. Dependencies stay cached while source changes.

front: Why combine `apt-get update` and `install` in one RUN?
back: A separately cached `update` layer keeps stale package lists, so later installs fail or get old versions. Also delete `/var/lib/apt/lists/*` in the same RUN.
Use COPY by default. ADD also fetches URLs (use `--checksum`), clones git repos and auto-extracts local tar archives — use it only on purpose.
`npm ci` installs exactly the lockfile, fails if it's out of sync with package.json, and starts from a clean `node_modules` — reproducible builds.

front: Tools to see what's inside an image
back: `docker history` (layers, sizes, instructions), `docker image inspect` (config, digests), `dive` (per-layer files, wasted space; `dive --ci` in pipelines).
